correctness.rationale: A length-bounded square sees at most three ones, and hence has zero ones or one per half. For mixed squares the central consecutive-one distance fixes the root length; fitting the external zero strings gives exactly the stated offset intervals, and summing the fit inequalities gives twice the root length at most n−1. Literal (length,offset) pairs are unique; equal-length intervals must be unioned, giving all four sorted-gap cases, including gaps of one. Anchoring an indexed word at a uniform one gives a uniform positive composition. Ties cost O(1) in the unscaled mean and the Lipschitz simplex grid has O(1/n) scaled error. The Dirichlet minimum and maximum means are 1/9 and 11/18; integrating the CDF (3t−1)^2 for the maximum on [1/3,1/2] gives the correction 1/36. The pushforward varies off the diagonals. Independent direct scans agreed on the full literal sets and counts for all 1,000 ordered gap triples in [1,10]^3, and computed exact means for n=3,4,5,8,12,20,30 (663 compositions). Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/589ded2e-b572-4146-af59-574172e61502/bounded_reproduce.py; output beside it as bounded_reproduce.out. These scans do not certify the all-size theorem; the proof does. The frozen verification describes finite internal checks, not formal verification.
